newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state, Thyssen, Krupp discuss merger plans.
newsitem.headline: German state, Thyssen, Krupp discuss merger plans.

text.p: The government of North Rhine-Westphalia state on Tuesday met representatives from steel giants Thyssen AG and Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp to discuss what is thought to be plans by Krupp to take over its rival, a government spokeswoman said.

A spokeswoman for the state economics ministry said state Premier Johannes Rau and Economics Minister Wolfgang Clement met with "various parties affected" by Krupp's plans to make a hostile bid for Thyssen.
"Economics Minister (Wolfgang) Clement was completely surprised by news of these merger plans. He knew nothing about it beforehand," she said.
Thyssen said late on Monday that it had information that its rival Krupp was preparing to make a hostile bid to Thyssen shareholders in a move to take control of the company.
Officials from North Rhine-Westphalia state, controlled by a coalition of Social Democrats (SPD) and environmentalist Greens, cancelled plans on Tuesday to travel to Potsdam near Berlin.
But the state government declined to make any official comment on the events.
